provider: 1fichier — registered free account, 5 TB of temporary storage with FTP + API

free_tier.stated: Registered (free) tier: '5 TB of temporary storage', folder sharing, remote upload, FTP upload, and API access. Paid ladder: Premium Light 500 GB €10/yr, 1000 GB €20/yr, Premium €54/yr with 4 TB cold storage, Premium GOLD €108/yr with 10 TB.

per_object_cap.stated: Per-file cap on free tier is not 300 GB

retention.stated: Retention is the killer, quoted: 'Retention: 30 days after upload, or 90 days after the last qualified access'

egress.terms: Downloads are unlimited on the free tier but ad/wait-gated and speed-limited, with a human-verification step; Premium removes ads and gives 300 GB per file and unlimited speed. Free-tier egress is 'unmetered but shaped' — the shaping, not the bytes, is the limit.

tooling: Documented public API plus FTP upload and remote upload (URL pull). rclone has no native 1fichier backend, so this is wrapper/API territory — the API is the client.
chaining: The multiplier is real and already known to the corpus: free accounts are email-only, and 5 TB per account is the largest genuinely-free quota found in this slot. Cross-referenced against dossier A (1fichier already appears there as 'free registered account (FTP + REST API)').

limits_note: Retention is the killer, quoted: 'Retention: 30 days after upload, or 90 days after the last qualified access'. Per-file cap on free tier is not 300 GB (that is Premium Light); free-tier file size is lower and undocumented on this page — unverified. 5 TB is 'temporary storage', not durable.
reliability_note: 1fichier/DStorage is a carrier with its own transit, so egress is not a marginal cost for them — which is why the free 5 TB survives where others died. The 30/90-day retention clock is the practical failure mode: it is a staging area, not an archive.
